objectives: Segment pr-words into phonemes before spelling.
Write p and r in the correct order for the initial blend.
Spell pram, press, print and prop accurately.
Read each spelling back to check the vowel and ending.
concepts: Encoding maps heard phonemes to graphemes in order.
Both /p/ and /r/ must be represented in a pr-word.
The vowel and ending determine the rest of the spelling.
Read-back helps detect missing letters or an incorrect vowel.

definitions.definition: Represent spoken sounds with written graphemes.
Separate a spoken word into phonemes in order.
Read a written word after spelling it to check it matches the target.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct pam when the target is pram.
workedExamples.solution: Add r after p to represent the second consonant: pram.

commonMistakes: Leaving out r and spelling pram as pam.
Confusing the short vowels in pram, press and prop.
Reversing p and r in the initial blend.
Not reading the completed word back.
keyTakeaways: Segment the full word before writing.
Keep p and r in order at the beginning.
Use the correct vowel and ending for each word.
Read the spelling back and self-correct.

answerKeys.explanation: Pram represents all four phonemes in order.
The onset is p followed by r.
The spelling must represent /r/ in the blend.
Press uses e for the short /e/ sound.
Pam omits the /r/ sound from pram.
Segmentation identifies all sounds before writing.
Pram and prop share pr but have different rimes.
Read-back helps verify the full spelling.
Press uses e and double s at the end.
The blend is written pr in that order.
The r represents the second consonant in the onset.
